text:
anya: Quick heads up — intermittent quality regression after converting Llama3 vocab to Mistral-style tokenizer. Probable token aliasing + KV-cache offset. Repro below, pinging eng-ml.

matt: ugh. can you paste a minimal repro and a couple of failing inputs?

anya: repro is tiny. load the converted tokenizer we use in model-converter v0.7.2 and compare token ids/logits vs native Llama tokenizer. gist: sometimes tokens at byte-boundaries map to nearby ids.

anya: ```python
# minimal repro
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM
conv = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('llama3-converted-mistral')
native = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('llama3-native')
p = "Here's an example: I'm testing tokenization."
print(conv.tokenize(p))
print([conv.convert_tokens_to_ids(t) for t in conv.tokenize(p)])
print(native.tokenize(p))
print([native.convert_tokens_to_ids(t) for t in native.tokenize(p)])
```

anya: logs show token_a: 423 vs 425, token_b: 198 vs 200 for the same subword sequence. embedding dot between returned ids drops ~0.02 for affected tokens.

raj: assigning to me to run a larger eval. I'll run the 1k prompt compare on ded10. also will test q4_0 quantized pipeline to see amplification.

deploy-bot: deploy model-converter v0.7.2 -> staging completed (2024-07-15T12:03:21Z) :rocket:

sylvia: I saw a similar pattern when we previously swapped merges.json — punctuation-adjacent merges can shift by 1-2 ids if byte offsets are handled differently. check tokenizer.backend and special tokens. Also verify offsets via tokenizer.encode_plus(return_offsets_mapping=True).

anya: confirmed that offsets differ at boundary bytes for tokens with apostrophes and hyphens. quick diff: "I'm" -> conv ids [54, 423] vs native [54, 425] (second subtoken shifted +2).

matt: plan: 1) run 1k eval measuring per-token cross-entropy and token-id mismatch rate, 2) check KV cache alignment by forcing long prefix and comparing next-token probs, 3) if repro small, patch converter to preserve native merges file.

raj: starting evaluate now. config: 1k prompts from prompt-corpus/v2, length 128, compare native vs converted on CPU (tokenizer) + GPU model. posting results in ~30m.

sylvia: also double-check rotary phase usage. If token-id -> position mapping is off by a small delta, sin/cos lookup can misalign and amplify regression for long-context.

anya: created issue https://redwood.internal/eng-ml/issues/4123 "token aliasing after converter v0.7.2" and added repro + tiny dataset. assigned to eng-ml. suggested temporary workaround: force tokenizer to load original merges/vocab file or apply alias remap table at converter output.

raj: results: 1k eval finished. token-id mismatch rate: 3.1% overall, concentrated on punctuation and contraction subtokens. avg perplexity delta: +0.8% native->converted. q4_0 quantized test increased perplexity delta to +1.9% and produced some small logit skew on top predictions. attaching CSV to issue.

matt: interesting — quantization amplifying makes sense because small embedding differences get noisier. thanks for test.

anya: agreed. rollback staging converter to v0.7.1 for now. Will schedule a short patch: either remap problematic ids or regenerate tokenizer using native merges.

ops-bot: rollback executed: model-converter v0.7.2 -> v0.7.1 (2024-07-15T13:22:05Z) :white_check_mark:

matt: next steps — raj to run a targeted ablation on merges vs byte-level offset handling; sylvia to prototype alias-table remap; anya to coordinate release notes and add regression alert in Redwood Optimize evals.

anya: thanks all. adding follow-ups to the issue and will update the rollout doc once we have a patch. :handshake:
